Torrenting remains one of the fastest and most efficient ways to share and download large files, but it also comes with some unique privacy and security concerns. Your internet service provider can see when you’re using P2P networks, malicious files can sometimes find their way into downloads, and your online activity may be exposed to third parties if you’re not properly protected.

description:
Microsoft has released the optional July 2026 preview update KB5101684 for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. The most significant improvement in this patch is a performance boost for Windows 11’s Start menu and taskbar, but how much of a difference you’ll actually notice will depend on the age and hardware of your PC.

Update KB5101684 also introduces usability improvements to File Explorer, like displaying file sizes in MBs and GBs instead of just KBs, which better reflects file sizes at a glance. Windows Search is also improved, with better performance and results when finding the files you’re looking for—even with search terms containing typos.

title: Windows 11’s optional July update speeds up the Start menu and taskbar

We’re now heading into August and the issue of updated Secure Boot certificates still hasn’t been resolved for all Windows users. description:
I’ve built a PC with just a single Craftsman screwdriver. I didn’t like doing it.

If I could go back in time to that first build, I’d invest $30 to $50 in useful tools. The right kit reduces the need to retrace your steps, puzzle over what you’re looking at, and even replace damaged parts.

Learn from my mistakes and don’t shortchange yourself on your toolset. (Especially if you’re already spending way more on your PC parts.) Below is a list of my absolute top five recommendations, in descending order of importance. But each one is very affordable, so you may as well get all of them.

1 – Magnetic screwdriver set
title: I’ve built PCs for years. These 5 cheap tools make every build suck less
